about: Product Dashboard (dashboard.html) query list. Each query runs once over the last 90 complete UTC days: replace "<START>" with the first day's 00:00:00 UTC and "<END>" with yesterday 23:59:59 UTC as epoch seconds (numbers, not strings). 'chart' goes to query_amplitude_data's chart param, 'definition' to its definition param; always pass projectId 773708, groupByLimit as given and timeSeriesLimit equal to it. Save each raw tool result as <raw-dir>/<id>.json, then run node scripts/build-dashboard.mjs <raw-dir>. Overview shows only the paid segment; the all/free segments stay in the queries so every response is large enough to be saved to a file. Lesson queries (les_*): funnels from a subscriber's first-ever node (anm_conv_page_viewed, nth time 1, event-time rc_subscription_status paid, start_version 2.8+/2.9+/3.) to completed lessons (anm_c_lesson_completed) within 7 days, per first-node day. Activation queries (pa_*) cover 17 Monday weeks instead: replace "<WSTART>" with the Monday of yesterday's week minus 16 weeks, 00:00:00 UTC ("<END>" is still yesterday 23:59:59 UTC). Each runs once per entry event: *_sub = first-ever rc_subscription_event, *_web = first-ever rc_non_subscription_purchase_event of users without a subscription before 28 Sep (the bulk move of existing web subscribers); pa_s = lesson start buttons within 7 days, pa_c = 1…10 anm_c_lesson_completed within 7 days, pa_f = 1…3 within 24 hours. 13 segments (all, iOS, Android, the 10 countries) keep each response large enough to be saved to a file.

rc.how: RevenueCat get-chart-data project proj9cc11412, chart actives, resolution 1 (week), segment store, start_date = first day, end_date = yesterday. Write <raw-dir>/rc.json as {"weeks":[{"d":"YYYY-MM-DD","app_store":N,"play_store":N}]} — one row per returned cohort (cohort epoch -> UTC date), App Store and Play Store values only; map segment indices by the response's segments list (order varies between calls). Skip Stripe (frozen at 10488 since 2026-09-28) and Paddle (legacy, flat).
